title: Fringe-SGC: Counting Subgraphs with Fringe Vertices
problem: Subgraph counting algorithms cannot handle large patterns due to exponential computational complexity
motivation: Subgraph counting is essential for cybersecurity, drug discovery, social networks, and NLP applications
method: The algorithm separates subgraph counting—finding how many times a graph pattern appears—into two steps: identifying instances of the core subgraph pattern, then computing occurrences by examining the fringe vertices (the adjacent vertices and edges around each match) using set operations to efficiently determine which connections belong to which instance.
key_novelty: By decomposing subgraph counting into core-pattern identification and separate fringe-vertex occurrence computation, the algorithm can exactly count larger patterns than previously possible, with GPU acceleration for patterns where fringe computation is the bottleneck.
contributions: Introduces Fringe-SGC technique for subgraph counting
Enables counting of previously infeasible large patterns
Achieves significant GPU speedups over SOTA
limitations: Performance gains most significant on patterns with many fringes; limited to exact counting
